function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL and retrieves data as specified by the parameters. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL to which the GET request is sent. It is expected to be a well-formed HTTP or HTTPS URL.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: The Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

headers.description: A dictionary of HTTP headers to send with the request. Each key-value pair represents a header name and its value.

timeout.description: The number of seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up, as a float, or a (connect_timeout, read_timeout) tuple. This is a float type value.

lat.description: Latitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

lon.description: Longitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters to append to the URL for the GET request.

allow_redirects.description: Determines if HTTP redirections (301, 302, etc.) should be followed.

auth.description: A tuple representing the user credentials for HTTP authentication, typically in the form of (username, password).

cert.description: Path to an SSL certificate file to verify the peer, or a tuple of (certificate file, key file).

cookies.description: A dictionary of cookies to send with the request. The key is the cookie name and the value is the cookie value.

http.description: URL of the proxy for HTTP requests.

https.description: URL of the proxy for HTTPS requests.

proxies.description: A dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy.

stream.description: If True, the response content will not be downloaded immediately but streamed.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate or not, or a path to a CA bundle if verification is needed.

Sure thing! Where you’ll find the best place to order a cake really depends on what kind of cake you’re after, how much time you’ve got, and whether you’re looking for something local or nationwide. Below is a quick guide to help you decide—and a few concrete places you might consider: | What You Need | Best Option | How to Order | Tips | |---------------|-------------|--------------|------| | **Custom, hand‑decorated cake** | Local artisan bakeries | • Search “custom cake near me” on Google Maps or Yelp.
• Call ahead (most accept phone orders).
• Many now offer online booking through their own site or Instagram DM. | • Give at least 1–2 weeks notice for custom designs.
• Bring a photo reference if you have a specific look in mind. | | **Same‑day delivery** | Food‑delivery apps (DoorDash, Uber Eats, Grubhub, Postmates, Instacart) | • Open the app, search “cake” or “bakery.”
• Filter by “delivery” and “rating.” | • Delivery fees vary—look for free delivery promotions.
• Check estimated delivery time; most apps show it in real time. | | **Pre‑made, ready‑to‑eat cakes** | Grocery chains (Walmart, Target, Kroger, Safeway, Publix) | • Visit the bakery section in-store or order online via the store’s website/app. | • Most stores ship within 24 h if you’re in the same state.
• Some offer “pick‑up” for faster service. | | **Specialty flavors (gluten‑free, vegan, keto)** | Specialty bakeries & health‑food stores | • Look for “gluten‑free bakery” + your city.
• Many have dedicated sections on their sites for dietary needs. | • Verify ingredient lists if you have allergies.
• Some bakeries offer “build‑your‑own” kits for home baking. | | **Large orders (weddings, corporate events)** | Dedicated cake designers (e.g., Cake Boss, BakeShare, local wedding planners) | • Use their websites to submit a design brief and quote request.
• Some allow live video consultations. | • Get a written contract covering size, flavor, delivery date, and cancellation policy. | | **Budget friendly** | Discount retailers (Costco, Sam’s Club) | • Buy a pre‑made cake from the bulk‑buy section.
• Many clubs ship to members’ homes. | • Check expiration dates carefully—bulk cakes often last longer. | | **National brands** | Online marketplaces (Amazon, Walmart.com) | • Search “birthday cake” or “pre‑baked cake” on the site.
• Read customer photos and reviews. | • Shipping may take 3–7 days unless you opt for expedited shipping. | ### Quick Steps to Order Anywhere 1. **Decide on the type of cake** – custom vs. pre‑made, dietary restrictions, occasion. 2. **Choose a platform** – local bakery (phone or website), food‑delivery app, grocery chain, or national retailer. 3. **Place the order** – fill out the online form or call the bakery. Be clear about: * Size (number of servings) * Flavor & filling * Frosting & decorations * Delivery address & time window 4. **Confirm payment** – most online platforms let you pay upfront; many bakeries accept cash on delivery if you prefer. 5. **Track the order** – if you ordered online, you’ll usually get a tracking link or status updates via email/SMS. --- #### Want a Specific Recommendation? If you tell me your city or ZIP code, I can pull up a list of highly rated local bakeries, including their phone numbers, websites, and average delivery times. Just drop your location here, and I’ll do the legwork for you! Happy cake hunting! 🍰
